hypothesis: The architectural register-file second read port is the culprit: regfile.rs2_data is not returning the value of the register addressed by rs2_addr (it is effectively stuck at 0 or mis-addressed, and/or its top-level connection in rv32i5.sv to id_stage.rs2_data is broken). Because every R-type ALU instruction gets rs2=0 at operand B, results collapse to the rs1 operand (t02_alu_r x4 0xb->0x3 for OR, x16/x17 SLT/SLTU ->0), and the t05_forward chain degenerates into 'each instruction writes back its own rs1' (x2=0x5, x3=0xf=x2_old, x5=0xa, x13=0x2a) since the forwarded register was never actually consumed. The same dead rs2 operand feeds the EX branch comparator, so the loop-exit condition in bench_ooo_overlap64 never becomes true, the PC walks through the 0xa5a5a5a5 fill region (0xc24..0xc5c) and the ECALL never retires, leaving halted=0 until the 6000-cycle timeout. The few immediate-form failures (t03_alu_imm x3 expected 0xfffff7ff got 0x000007fe) are a residual part of the same operand-B formation: the I-immediate reaching EX is a zero-extended, LSB-cleared slice {instr[31:21],1'b0} instead of the sign-extended instr[31:20]. Rounds 1-5 all rewrote the ALU B-mux polarity, the id_stage immediate expression, the ID/EX payload capture and the wb/regfile commit path, but never fixed the register file's second read port or its top-level wiring, which is why the identical R-type/forwarding/branch failures persist. This is the majority root cause.
constraints: Keep the top-level rv32i5 port list fixed: clk, rst_n, imem_addr, imem_rdata, dmem_valid, dmem_we, dmem_addr, dmem_wdata, dmem_be, dmem_rdata, dbg_reg_addr, dbg_reg_data, halted, exit_code.
regfile.rs1_data and regfile.rs2_data must be combinational reads of the register addressed by rs1_addr/rs2_addr; x0 always reads 0; write port (we/waddr/wdata from wb_stage) is unchanged.
dbg_reg_addr/dbg_reg_data: combinational read of architectural register (x0=0), independent of forwarding; must not be broken by the fix.
Forwarding semantics unchanged: EX/MEM (forward=1) priority over MEM/WB (forward=2); never forward when rd==x0 or source field==x0; only when valid && reg_write && !mem_read(for EX/MEM).
I-immediate must be sign-extended from instr[31:20] (not zero-extended, not LSB-cleared); S/B/U/J immediates unchanged in mapping.
No new pipeline stages, no extra wait states, no hardcoded values, no changes to spec/TB/scoring; if_stage/imem_addr word-aligned; dmem_valid = mem_stage.mem_dmem_valid & rst_n & ~halted.
Module names of the 8 frozen modules must not change; only internal wiring/logic of the named files may change.
verification_targets: bench_ooo_overlap64: halted becomes 1 with exit_code==0 well before the 6000-cycle timeout (loop exit branch resolves, PC no longer pinned at 0x00000028 or walking 0xc24..0xc5c).
regression: no new failures introduced in base suite; fb/forwarding EX/MEM priority still correct.

Round 4: ALU B-operand mux polarity inverted — applied, same failures remain.
